title: RNCBIGene: NCBI Gene annotation in parquet
text: Bioconductor’s annotation system functioned well decade pivotal resource analysis tool development. See AnnotationDbi documentation details. AnnotationDbi packages based use SQLite manage organism-specific vocabularies resolve queries mappings identifier sets. example, learn Gene Ontology annotations gene ORMDL3 Homo sapiens: RNCBIGene takes different approach: instead organism-specific SQLite databases, NCBI Gene annotation organisms lives set Apache Parquet files NSF Open Storage Network bucket. Queries run persistent duckdb connection reads remote parquet directly, pushing filters column selections network layer data lands R. open_ncbi_gene() function returns lazy dplyr::tbl; user composes filter(), select(), collect() calls remote dplyr backend. duckdb httpfs extension required remote parquet access cached permanently tools::R_user_dir("RNCBIGene", "data") rather temporary directory, downloaded per machine. cache location can overridden setting DUCKDB_EXTENSION_DIRECTORY environment variable loading package. purpose package provide pin-compatible replacements AnnotationDbi packages. package explores opportunities simplification performance enhancement arising adoption Parquet Arrow annotation representation interrogation.
code: library(org.Hs.eg.db) go_orm = AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db, key="ORMDL3", keytype="SYMBOL",     columns=c("GO", "ENTREZID")) head(go_orm) ##   SYMBOL         GO EVIDENCE ONTOLOGY ENTREZID ## 1 ORMDL3 GO:0002903      IMP       BP    94103 ## 2 ORMDL3 GO:0005515      IPI       MF    94103 ## 3 ORMDL3 GO:0005783      IDA       CC    94103 ## 4 ORMDL3 GO:0005789      IEA       CC    94103 ## 5 ORMDL3 GO:0005886      TAS       CC    94103 ## 6 ORMDL3 GO:0006665      IEA       BP    94103 library(RNCBIGene) library(dplyr) lkor = open_ncbi_gene("gene2go", taxid=9606L) |>   filter(GeneID==94103) |> collect() |> as.data.frame() DT::datatable(lkor)

title: RNCBIGene: NCBI Gene annotation in parquet
text: open_ncbi_gene() returns lazy dplyr::tbl backed duckdb VIEW remote parquet file. data fetched collect() called. Predicates passed filter() column lists select() translated SQL pushed parquet read, requested rows columns travel wire. object lazy SQL-backed tbl – inspecting triggers small preview fetch load full dataset. Compose multi-step query collecting: interface works eight resources. Omitting taxid returns tbl spanning organisms:
code: tbl <- open_ncbi_gene("gene_info", taxid = 9606L) class(tbl) ## [1] "tbl_duckdb_connection" "tbl_dbi"               "tbl_sql"               ## [4] "tbl_lazy"              "tbl" open_ncbi_gene("gene_info", taxid = 9606L) |>   filter(Symbol %in% c("TP53", "ORMDL3", "BRCA1", "GSDMB")) |>   select(Symbol, GeneID, map_location, type_of_gene) |>   collect() ## # A tibble: 4 × 4 ##   Symbol GeneID map_location type_of_gene   ##   <chr>   <dbl> <chr>        <chr>          ## 1 TP53     7157 17p13.1      protein-coding ## 2 GSDMB   55876 17q21.1      protein-coding ## 3 ORMDL3  94103 17q21.1      protein-coding ## 4 BRCA1     672 17q21.31     protein-coding open_ncbi_gene("gene_orthologs") |>   filter(GeneID == 7157L) |>   # TP53 orthologs across all taxa   collect()

title: RNCBIGene: NCBI Gene annotation in parquet
text: NCBI Gene annotation organisms lives parquet files, switching species simply matter changing taxid. look Ensembl gene transcript identifiers mouse (Mus musculus, taxid 10090) gene Lilrb4a. quick symbol--Ensembl-gene lookup: full transcript-level picture join gene_info (filtered symbol) gene2ensembl entirely within duckdb – lazy tbls share connection, join pushed data collected: result reveals two distinct Ensembl gene models Lilrb4a – something two-step approach (Symbol -> one gene ID -> transcripts) missed. Joining directly GeneID returns Ensembl records gene single query.
code: mapIdsNG(keys = "Lilrb4a", keytype = "Symbol", column = "Ensembl",          taxid = 10090L) ##              Lilrb4a  ## "ENSMUSG00000112148" gene_info_mouse <- open_ncbi_gene("gene_info", taxid = 10090L) |>   dplyr::filter(.data[["Symbol"]] == "Lilrb4a") |>   dplyr::select(GeneID, Symbol)  open_ncbi_gene("gene2ensembl", taxid = 10090L) |>   dplyr::inner_join(gene_info_mouse, by = "GeneID") |>   dplyr::select(Symbol, Ensembl_gene_identifier,                 Ensembl_rna_identifier, Ensembl_protein_identifier) |>   dplyr::collect() ## # A tibble: 3 × 4 ##   Symbol  Ensembl_gene_identifier Ensembl_rna_identifier Ensembl_protein_ident…¹ ##   <chr>   <chr>                   <chr>                  <chr>                   ## 1 Lilrb4a ENSMUSG00000112148      ENSMUST00000218617.2   -                       ## 2 Lilrb4a ENSMUSG00000112148      ENSMUST00000078778.5   ENSMUSP00000077833.4    ## 3 Lilrb4a ENSMUSG00000062593      ENSMUST00000218123.2   ENSMUSP00000151827.2    ## # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​Ensembl_protein_identifier

what: Joining local data to remote annotation with join_ncbi_gene()
title: RNCBIGene: NCBI Gene annotation in parquet
text: join_ncbi_gene() uploads local data frame duckdb session temporary table returns lazy join remote NCBI Gene resource. sides join run duckdb; caller decides select() collect(). Unmatched keys (XyZZY) appear NA annotation columns default join type "left". Switch type = "inner" drop .
code: local_df <- data.frame(Symbol = c("ORMDL3", "TP53", "BRCA1", "GSDMB", "XyZZY"))  join_ncbi_gene(local_df, by = "Symbol", taxid = 9606L) |>   select(Symbol, GeneID, map_location, type_of_gene) |>   collect() ## # A tibble: 5 × 4 ##   Symbol GeneID map_location type_of_gene   ##   <chr>   <dbl> <chr>        <chr>          ## 1 TP53     7157 17p13.1      protein-coding ## 2 GSDMB   55876 17q21.1      protein-coding ## 3 ORMDL3  94103 17q21.1      protein-coding ## 4 BRCA1     672 17q21.31     protein-coding ## 5 XyZZY      NA NA           NA

what: Enriching a GeneID table with GO terms and RefSeq identifiers
title: RNCBIGene: NCBI Gene annotation in parquet
text: multiple annotation resources needed, requires separate join back original data frame. GO terms RefSeq identifiers one--many relationships GeneID: three genes yield hundreds GO annotations hundreds transcript/protein pairs. Joining resources single query produce Cartesian product; correct pattern two independent joins. Start local data frame Entrez IDs: GO terms – one row per gene-GO pair: RefSeq identifiers – one row per gene-transcript pair (excluding entries RNA accession): result shares GeneID key original local_ids data frame can used independently merged dplyr::left_join() collecting, depending downstream analysis.
